title: Uptime Catalyst: 45-day Tactical Plan & Signal Probes
content:
Context:
We need a fast, instrumented pilot to validate cross-team processes for SLO alignment, signal hygiene, and rapid mitigation. This doc is a tactical 45-day plan (3 x 2-week sprints + buffer) to run the pilot across platform, serving runtime, SRE, and product console teams.

Why this is different:
- Narrow scope: pick 2 customer-facing routes (chat-generate and embeddings-index) to reduce blast radius.
- Focus on signal probes (small synthetic checks + canary traffic) rather than full productization.
- Treat the pilot as an experiment: clear hypothesis, metrics, decision gates.

Pilot hypothesis:
If we standardize a small set of SLOs, telemetry dashboards, and an on-call mitigation playbook for the two routes, then we can reduce incident-to-detection time by >= 30% and reduce false-positive alert noise by >= 40% during the pilot window.

Scope (explicit):
- Services: hosted-api route: /v1/generate-chat, embeddings service: /v1/embeddings (customer tier: standard).
- Telemetry: latency, p95/p99, error-rate (5xx), KV-cache hit rate, GPU queue length, model-fallback occurrences, prefix-cache hit ratio.
- Owners: platform-engineering (signal infra), serving-runtime (runtime traces & metrics), eng-sre (alerting & runbooks), product-hosted-api (route owners).
- Exclusions: Dedicated & Private customers; rollout to other routes outside pilot window.

SLO candidates (for pilot only):
- Availability SLO: 99.9% of requests return 2xx within 30 seconds (measurement: rolling 7d).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for small requests (<=128 tokens), p99 < 1.2s (observed at edge).
- Error SLO: 99.95% of requests without backend 5xx or model-fallback events.
Note: numeric targets are draft — we will tune on day 0 signals.

Signal probes (what we'll run):
1) Synthetic requester (every 10s): small, medium, long sequences to three regions. Measure latencies and model-fallback rate.
2) Canary traffic (1% of production on route only): mirrored to pilot cluster; golden path expected to match baseline.
3) KV-cache warmup probe: hit prefix sets to validate caching behavior pre-peak.
4) GPU queue probe: push small burst and measure queue growth + eviction.
5) Error fuzz probe: intentionally send malformed prompt to ensure error classification and no noisy paging.

Instrumentation checklist (minimum viable):
- Per-route tokenized latencies (edge->runtime->model) (serving-runtime)
- SLI exporters for prefix/KV cache hit ratio (platform-engineering)
- Model-fallback counter + context tags (model name, quantization profile) (serving-runtime)
- Alert rules in Alertmanager (eng-sre): severity: page (P0), notify slack #ops-oncall; severity: ticket (P2), notify #platform-notify
- SLO dashboards in Grafana: 7d rolling, latency histograms, error waterfall (platform-engineering)

Measurement plan & dashboards:
- Daily dashboard snapshot automated (email + slack) at 9:00 PT with 24h rolling and 7d delta.
- Weekly executive note: signal performance + experiment findings.
- Ad-hoc postmortem if any P0 occurs.

Runbook sketch (to iterate into formal runbook):
- Signal: p99 latency > 2x baseline for 5m across regions -> Runbook steps: 1) check GPU queue and prefix cache metrics; 2) fail-over to lower-capacity variant (if policy allowed); 3) scale temporary burst pool (if Dedicated capacity available) OR toggle sampling rate for heavy prompts; 4) engage serving-runtime oncall.
- Signal: model-fallback rate spike -> rollback last model rollout OR route to cached model variant.

Staffing & rota (45d):
- Weekdays: 1x platform-engineer (day), 1x serving-runtime engineer (day), oncall SRE rotation (night).
- Sprint-level owners: Sprint 1 (signal plumbing): Miguel Ortega; Sprint 2 (SLO tuning + dashboards): Aisha Patel; Sprint 3 (mitigation & runbook run-through): Priya Desai.
- Escalation: if P0 not mitigated in 30m, escalate to Head of Eng (Liam Chen) and Product PM.

Cadence & milestones:
- Day 0 (kickoff): align owners, finalize SLO targets, enable synthetic probes in staging.
- Sprint 1 (0-14d): telemetry plumbing, synthetic probes active in staging, baseline capture.
- Sprint 2 (15-30d): enable probes in canary, iterate SLO thresholds, dashboard creation, runbook drafts.
- Sprint 3 (31-45d): stress run (2x synthetic load), mitigation rehearsals, finalize decision memo and next-steps recommendation.
- Decision gate (day 46): accept (scale program) | iterate (extend pilot 30d) | rollback (abandon changes). Decision based on measured hypothesis metrics.

Success criteria (quantitative + qualitative):
- Quantitative: incident-to-detection time reduced >= 30% (compared to prior 90d avg) OR alert noise (P2/P3 rate) reduced >= 40% on pilot routes.
- Qualitative: teams report clearer ownership, runbook is actionable in tabletop, dashboards are readable and used in standups.

Communication plan:
- Daily short standup (15m) with owners M-F during Sprint 1 & 2.
- Weekly demo to broader reliability guild (Friday).
- Post-pilot summary doc + 1-pager for execs.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Canary traffic causes customer visible regressions. Mitigation: start with 0.1% ramp, have automatic kill-switch based on error-rate delta > 5x baseline.
- Risk: Too many signals -> alert fatigue. Mitigation: threshold tuning and temporary muting by severity and confidence score.
- Risk: Telemetry gaps delay decisions. Mitigation: define minimal SLI exporters and enforcement on day 0.

Open questions (to resolve at kickoff):
- Do we allow automatic model-fallback rollbacks for pilot or require manual approval?
- Baseline window: use last 30d production or 7d rolling? (propose 30d for stability).
- Who owns the 24/7 kill-switch and where is it documented?

Checklist (day 0 -> day 3):
- [ ] Confirm owners and primary contacts
- [ ] Create Grafana folder + baseline panels
- [ ] Deploy synthetic probes to staging (config repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-probes/pull/14)
- [ ] Create Alertmanager rules and routing
- [ ] Draft initial runbook and put into /docs/runbooks/uptime-catalyst

Next immediate actions (Aisha):
- Book kickoff: invite SRE, serving-runtime, platform-engineering, product-hosted-api (suggested: 2026-03-16 10:00 PT)
- Open temporary pilot channel (#uptime-catalyst) and invite listed collaborators
- Raise PR for synthetic probes and tag Miguel for review

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep SLO targets intentionally conservative so pilot shows wins by improving detection and noise reduction, rather than chasing perfect latency numbers.
- Document every small tweak in the pilot log — learning velocity > perfect instrumentation.
- We should make the decision memo template now so end-of-pilot writeup is quick.

Related tickets & references: SRE-789 (alerting), CON-2456 (pilot charter), ops-probes PR (#14), reliability-playbook PR/112.
